title: Lou Henry's band personnel and the thrill of the Savoy
summary: He names those he remembers in Lou Henry's band and recalls how glamorous working at the Savoy was.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Do you remember who else was in that band?

The reed section... I know who the reed section was. It was Bob Holmes, and the tenor player's name was Tramp -- he's dead now...Trent. Not Alfonso Trent. He was a tenor player. Anyway, let me see. There was Anderson... I don't remember who else was in the trumpets.
But there were two trumpets, though.

Yeah. Yeah, there was another man(?)... And Lou Henry himself played trombone. And that's about all I can remember. I don't know who was drumming or who played piano. But I enjoyed it. Boy, just think. Me working at
the Savoy! With all those pretty hostesses and things around there... Man, I enjoyed working there.

After three months, I had to leave...there was nothing like it. See, where you go to work on a job, and you open up and you sit down and you're ready to go to sleep, and then you're put in a place where all this life was around you, and all this beauty and one thing or another, and everybody comin' there, and looking up at you... That was the place to be.
